patients.summary: High school math teacher with young-onset Parkinson disease and long-standing iron deficiency from heavy periods who joins in 2019; HHT is diagnosed in 2021, then restless legs, functional aphonia and GAD after a rupture with her son, hookworm after a volunteer trip to Brazil, benzodiazepine withdrawal when alprazolam runs out, and an urticarial transfusion reaction during an ED transfusion for HHT nosebleeds.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
40F here to establish. Moved her care from a practice in the Pioneer Valley she'd been at for years; wanted someone she could actually reach. Records requested.

PMH:
- Parkinson disease, young onset. Dx 2017 by outside neurology, who still follows her and writes the carbidopa-levodopa. Says it works well, she rarely notices anything on her doses. Sees them roughly yearly.
- Iron deficiency anemia, put down to heavy periods. Periods regular, heavy, the first two days especially. Has been on OTC ferrous sulfate for years, takes it with a vitamin C tab. Never had IV iron. No GYN workup she can recall.
- Nosebleeds since she was a teenager, a few a month, worse in winter. Cauterized once at 25. Father has the same and was told he had AVMs in his lungs. A paternal aunt also bleeds from the nose.
- Allergic rhinitis, tree pollen and dust. Loratadine when needed.

PSH: nasal cautery age 25.
Meds: carbidopa-levodopa 25-100 1 tab TID; ferrous sulfate 325 daily w/ vit C; loratadine 10 prn.
Allergies: NKDA. Shellfish -> itching and hives. Tree pollen, dust mites.
FHx: father nosebleeds + lung AVMs; paternal aunt nosebleeds; mother hypothyroid, generalized anxiety; son (12) has ADHD.
SH: teaches high school math. Married; lives in Sunderland with husband and her son (son is from her first marriage, his dad lives out of state). Vegetarian. Never smoked. 1-2 glasses of wine a week. PHQ-2 0.

ROS: tired by late afternoon most days, which she has gotten used to. No chest pain, no melena or hematochezia, no syncope.

Exam: well appearing, slightly pale conjunctivae. HEENT otherwise unremarkable. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft, NT. No edema. Neuro: no tremor at rest today, gait normal, speech normal.

A/P:
1. Iron deficiency anemia, chronic. CBC, iron studies today. Continue ferrous sulfate. Will discuss GYN once I see where she is.
2. Parkinson disease - per neurology. Will ask for their notes.
3. Recurrent epistaxis with a strong family story - noted.
4. Allergic rhinitis - loratadine prn.
5. HM: CMP, lipids, TSH; HCV and HIV screening (consented). Due for first mammogram - ordered. Pap/HPV per old records.
RTC for annual next fall, sooner prn.

documents.title: Your recent lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Paula,

Your labs are back. Your hemoglobin is 10.9 and your iron stores (ferritin) are low, so the iron deficiency is still there despite the daily tablets. Kidney, liver, thyroid and cholesterol results are all normal, and the hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative.

Keep taking the iron with the vitamin C. One tip: iron can blunt how well levodopa is absorbed, so take the iron at least two hours away from your carbidopa-levodopa doses. We'll recheck in the spring.

The radiology scheduling line should be calling you about the mammogram.

documents.body:
Received 38 pages by fax from patient's previous primary care office (release signed 9/10/19). Scanned to media.

Contents: office notes 2014-2019, lab reports, immunization record, cervical screening.
Highlights flagged for PCP:
- Pap with HPV 06/2018: NILM, HPV negative.
- Tdap 08/2012.
- Several CBCs 2015-2019, hemoglobin running 10s to 11s, on oral iron.
- Neurology correspondence 2017 re: new Parkinson diagnosis, carbidopa-levodopa started by neurology.

PCP reviewed and signed 9/25.

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Came after school for flu shot. No fever today, no prior reactions. Shellfish allergy noted, not relevant to this vaccine. Quadrivalent flu 0.5 mL IM left deltoid, lot and expiration in MAR. VIS reviewed. Waited 15 min, fine.

documents.title: Neurology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Re: Paula Wisniewski, DOB 03/09/1979. Seen 11/19/2019.

Thank you for taking over her primary care. Paula has young-onset Parkinson disease diagnosed here in 2017, with an excellent and sustained response to levodopa. She reports no wearing off between doses, no dyskinesia, no falls, no hallucinations, no constipation of note. Sleep is fair. She is teaching full time.

Medications: carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 one tablet three times daily; ferrous sulfate; loratadine as needed.

Examination (on medication): alert, fluent speech, normal facial expression. No rest or postural tremor. Tone normal in all limbs. Finger taps and foot taps full amplitude without decrement. Arises from chair without arms. Gait with normal stride and arm swing; pull test negative.

Impression: Parkinson disease, well controlled on current dose.
Plan: no changes. Prescription renewed for a year. Return in 12 months or sooner if new symptoms.

Outside neurology

documents.title: Iron timing question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, quick question. I take my first carbidopa-levodopa at 6:30 before school, then around noon and 6. When is the best time for the iron? I used to take it with breakfast with everything else.

documents.title: RE: Iron timing question
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Paula, per Dr.'s note: mid-morning (around 9-10 if you can manage it at school) or at bedtime both work well, as long as it's about 2 hours from a levodopa dose. Keep the vitamin C with it. Let us know if your stomach doesn't tolerate it.

documents.title: Appointment change
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called pt re: her April in-person follow-up. Office converting routine visits to video for now. Pt agreeable, rescheduled to 5/12 video. She is teaching remotely from home. Lab slip will be at the lab entrance for her to get drawn after.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, pt at home, verbal consent. Two-way audio/video.

S: Teaching remotely, says the screen days wear her out more than the classroom. Still tired in the afternoons, about the same as last fall. Taking iron at bedtime now, away from her levodopa. Periods unchanged, still heavy. A couple of nosebleeds a month, short. Pollen season - eyes itchy, using loratadine most days this month. Neuro meds unchanged, no new symptoms.

O: Well appearing on video, conversational, no distress.

A/P:
- Iron deficiency anemia: CBC/iron studies at the lab this week. Continue ferrous sulfate.
- Allergic rhinitis, seasonal: loratadine daily through the season is fine.
- PD: per neurology.
F/u annual in fall.

documents.title: Lab result note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hgb and ferritin essentially unchanged from September, still iron deficient. Continue oral iron. Message sent to pt. Recheck at annual.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
41F annual. Back in the building teaching hybrid, masks all day, voice tired by Friday but fine.

Interval: no hospital visits. Fatigue unchanged. Heavy periods unchanged. Nosebleeds a few times a month, stop with pressure. Neurology follow-up due in November.

Meds: carbidopa-levodopa 25-100 TID, ferrous sulfate 325 daily (bedtime), loratadine prn.
Allergies: NKDA; shellfish; tree pollen, dust mites.
SH: unchanged. Never smoker. Wine 1-2/wk. PHQ-2 0.

Exam: NAD. Conjunctivae a little pale. Nasal mucosa without active bleeding. Thyroid normal. RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd benign. Skin no rash. No edema. Neuro: no tremor, gait normal.

A/P:
- Health maintenance: Tdap today (last 2012). Flu shot next month when clinic stock arrives. Mammogram ordered. Pap due 2023.
- Iron deficiency anemia: CBC, ferritin today. Continue iron.
- PD: stable per neurology.
- Allergic rhinitis: prn loratadine.
RTC 1 yr, sooner prn.

documents.title: Neurology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Re: Paula Wisniewski (DOB 03/09/1979), seen by video 11/17/2020 with a brief in-person exam the same afternoon.

Paula remains well on carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 three times daily. No end-of-dose wearing off, no involuntary movements, no falls or freezing. Mood good, sleep okay. Cognitively she reports no change. Tolerating the iron at bedtime away from her doses.

Exam on medication: normal speech and facial expression; no tremor; normal tone; rapid alternating movements brisk and symmetric; normal gait and turns; pull test negative.

Assessment: Parkinson disease, stable.
Plan: continue same. Annual follow-up.

Outside neurology
